companion.title: Collision detection for collaborative assembly operations on high-payload robots
companion.evidence: Publisher article page and registered metadata. Reported reductions/latencies in the paper are not used as labels in the calculations here.

evidence: Full original ZIP and all 80 bag files checked by checksum and ROS connection metadata. Read external + robot-end force streams and Boolean detector signals for all 55 numbered, documentation-linked CALPAK August events (17 August 3 and 38 August 4). The 25 remaining bags, including unnumbered and earlier sessions, are listed separately as file/connection evidence. The previous project record had decoded a prefix of one bag.
experiments: The two source log sheets specify speed override, pads, arm extension, orientation, and panel condition (with additional detector selection and notes where available). For 17 trials on August 3 the authors list a peak force, with no computation rule in that table. All 55 August fixture runs contain /external_ft_sensor and /coll_det_ee/force JointState effort arrays. The robot topic labels x, y, z, tx, ty, tz, sum_abs in the checked sample; the external JointState has no component names in that sample. The raw ROS arrays do not encode measurement units or a frame transform. We retain raw numerical units for triplet norms and do not swap axes or compare torque components as if they shared a load origin.
methods: Decode each archived ROS1 JointState using the message layout, retain publisher timestamp, recorder timestamp, and first six effort values. Separate reference clocks and robot/fixture axes. Compute per-topic median first 0.5 s as descriptive initial reference, without claiming physical unloaded bias. Report force-like and moment-like triplet norms; a descriptive event threshold is three consecutive samples above magnitude 20 in the baseline-subtracted first triplet. Boolean false-to-true events are counted using bag recorder stamps. If a flag was already true at start, the next observed rising edge is used. Differences are recorder-level alignment diagnostics, not hardware latency, injury thresholds or physical switch certificates.
checks: Complete coverage: 2,211,926 external-sensor messages and 840,895 robot EE force messages in the 55 documented trials. External median(header−bag) is +130.904 to +131.908 s and the robot EE median is −1.321 to −0.626 s. The median offsets differ by 131.548 to 133.082 s across each trial. With external axis lengths/units treated as archived, 16 of 17 original listed peaks fall within 15 numeric units of the raw first-triplet norm peak. The remaining 2022_08_03_calpak/3.bag lists 397 but the largest recorded norm is 240.6. This mismatch cannot establish whether metadata assignment or computation differs; preserve both. Detector flags and magnitude exceedances do not uniquely label first contact or steady contact.
reproduce: Python 3.12, NumPy, rosbags 0.11.10; python derive_collision.py data.zip OUTPUT_DIR. Uses one temporary extracted bag at a time; about 170 MB temporary space. All four channels decoded for each documented August trial. A separate ROS1 typestore deserialization of trial 3 independently checked both topic counts, norms and median timestamp offsets.
